## The `step-finish` `tokens`/`cost` already include the user message — so the `user` event is metrics-neutral

A concern came up: does surfacing the prompt as its own `user` event risk double-counting tokens/cost, or are the streamed metrics somehow off? Short answer: **no.** The user turn has no token/cost record of its own — it's already embedded in the assistant step's `input`/`cost`. The `user` event is a pure transcript/stream addition and changes no metric. Here's the proof, using one real `gpt-4o-mini` session (`ses_1861c075…`) captured both ways.

**Stream (`run --format json`) — `step_finish`:**
```json
{"type":"step-finish","tokens":{"total":13185,"input":13174,"output":11,"reasoning":0,"cache":{"write":0,"read":0}},"cost":0.0019827}
```
**`export` of the same session** agrees exactly: assistant message `tokens.input 13174`, `cost 0.0019827`; session-level `info.cost 0.0019827`, `info.tokens.input 13174`.

### 1. There is exactly one input-token figure in the whole transcript, and it's on the assistant step
In `export`, the **user message** (`msg_e79e3f8ca…`) is just `{"role":"user","parts":[{"type":"text","text":"\"say hello\""}]}` — **no `tokens`, no `cost`.** The assistant message (`msg_e79e3f904…`) has `parentID: "msg_e79e3f8ca…"`, i.e. its parent *is* that user message — one request→response turn. The only `input` count anywhere is the **13174** on that assistant step, so the user message's tokens can only be folded into it. If they were excluded they'd be counted nowhere — yet the model clearly read "say hello" to answer.

### 2. By construction, the user message is inside the request the provider counts
```
run.ts            session.prompt({ parts: [...files, { type:"text", text: message }] })   ← the prompt
prompt.ts:1121    persists those parts as the user message
prompt.ts:1439/51 msgs (incl. that user message as `lastUser`) → toModelMessagesEffect → messages: <model call>
session.ts:383    getUsage: inputTokens = usage.inputTokens   ← provider's count of the WHOLE prompt
```
`usage.inputTokens` is the provider's count of everything it received (system + tools + user message); `getUsage` takes it verbatim (minus cache). There is no code path where the user text reaches the model but escapes `usage.inputTokens`.

### 3. `cost` is a pure, exact function of those tokens
Formula at `session.ts:429-439`:
```
cost = input·Cin/1e6 + output·Cout/1e6 + cacheRead·Cr/1e6 + cacheWrite·Cw/1e6 + reasoning·Cout/1e6
```
gpt-4o-mini = `input 0.15` / `output 0.60` per 1M (cache = 0, reasoning = 0 here):
```
13174 · 0.15/1e6 = 0.0019761
   11 · 0.60/1e6 = 0.0000066
                  ───────────
                    0.0019827   ← exactly the reported cost
```
Reconstructed to the last digit ⇒ no separate "user-message cost" term. `cost` is inclusive of the user message iff `tokens.input` is, and §1–2 show it is.

### 4. Empirical clincher (model-independent)
Enlarge only the user message; system prompt + tools are identical across two fresh runs, so `Δinput` = the user message's tokens:
```bash
opencode --model=openai/gpt-4o-mini run --format json -- "say hello" \
  | grep -o '"input":[0-9]*'          # → ~13174 (baseline)

MSG=$(python3 -c "print('banana '*2000)")
opencode --model=openai/gpt-4o-mini run --format json -- "$MSG" \
  | grep -o '"input":[0-9]*'          # → ~13174 + ~2000
```
If `step-finish` didn't count the user message, the second `input` would stay ≈13174. It rises by ~2000 — that delta **is** the user message, counted in `step-finish`. (On a rerun you may see `cache.read > 0`; then compare `input + cache.read + cache.write`, since the system-prompt prefix can be cached but the changing user suffix can't.)

### Conclusion
The user turn carries no independent token/cost record — it lives inside the assistant step's `input` (13174) and the cost derived from it (0.0019827); the session totals equal that single step because this is a one-step run. **The `user` event is therefore purely additive to the stream — it

@I-shm Thank you for your testing!

The issue was when a CJK character (width 2, length 1) preceded a $skillname in the prompt, submission corrupted the reference — e.g. $w$webapp-testing instead of $webapp-testing. The extmark system stored positions as display-width offsets (Bun.stringWidth) but used them to slice() inputText with character offsets, so every preceding CJK char shifted the slice by one extra position.

Fix: Refactored skills to use type: "skill" (matching the @ agent/file pattern) instead of type: "text" with kind: "skill". The extmark submission loop only processes type: "text" parts, so skills bypass the display-width-offset slice() entirely. The SkillPart & SkillPartInput type was added to the SDK to fix this.

- Passed `bun typecheck`
- Passed all tests in 'bun test`
- Able to build locally and run properly
- All user testing from before is working + trying CJK characters seems to work properly now as well

## Research: Tool Count Impact on Reasoning Quality

I ran a multi-source investigation into the tool count problem. Key findings that may help inform the design direction:

### Hard Numbers

Research from BFCL benchmarks and production case studies shows:

| Tool Count | Accuracy | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ≤20 | 96%+ | BFCL v3 multi-step |
| 40 | ~88% | Production case study (Presenc.ai) |
| 80+ | 76% | BFCL v3, ~20% drop |
| 120+ | 30% | Production case study, specialized domain |

Both Anthropic and OpenAI officially recommend **<20 tools** per request. The accuracy drop is caused by **attention dilution** — not "can't find the tool". Even when the correct tool appears in the first 1024 tokens of the tool list, accuracy still drops 6.2% with 80+ tools present.

### Caching Does Not Solve This

Prompt caching (Anthropic 90% cost reduction, OpenAI similar) solves the **cost** problem but not the **reasoning quality** problem. Cached KV tensors are reused, not freed — the model still attends to all tool definitions. This is the key insight: the problem is not token cost, it is model accuracy.

### Existing Solutions in the Wild

| Approach | Used By | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Tool Search (single meta-tool) | Anthropic official docs | One `tool_search` replaces all tools |
| File-based discovery | Cursor | Tool descriptions in files, agent uses rg/jq |
| RAG retrieval | LangChain | Embed tool descriptions, retrieve top-K |
| Two-stage filtering | Academic (Tool Attention) | ISO scoring + prune, 47K→2.4K tokens |

### Broader Design: LRU + Always-Include + Discovery

The `mcp_lazy` / `mcp_search` approach in PR #12520 addresses MCP tools specifically. But the tool count problem extends beyond MCP — builtin tools, LSP tools, and skill descriptions all contribute to context bloat.

A complementary approach for **all tools** (not just MCP):

1. **Always-include set**: Core tools that every agent needs every turn (read, edit, write, shell, glob, grep, task, todo, skill, fetch) — ~12 tools, ~5K tokens
2. **LRU-based pruning**: Track tool usage per session. Inject only the top-N recently used tools on top of the always-include set. Target: ~25 total tools per request.
3. **Discovery meta-tool**: Similar to `mcp_search`, but for ALL hidden tools (including LSP, experimental, and rarely-used builtins).
4. **Bootstrapping period**: First 2-3 turns include all tools (no LRU), giving the model time to establish a working set before pruning kicks in.

### Key Risks to Address

- **Silent task failure**: Model won't call a discovery tool if it doesn't know a specific tool is missing. Mitigation: tool category hints in system prompt + generous bootstrapping period.
- **Discovery loops**: Rate-limit discovery calls. After 2 calls in 5 turns, auto-include all tools.
- **Subagent inheritance**: Subagents spawned via `task` need their own tool profiles, not just the parent's LRU set.
- **Tool-result replay**: Prior turns may reference tools that are now hidden. Need ghost entries for provider compatibility.

### Integration Point

The cleanest insertion point in current codebase is `src/session/tools.ts` `resolve()` — after collecting registry + MCP tools, before returning the final tool set. Usage tracking hooks into `src/session/processor.ts` where tool-call events are processed (line 377+, `value.name` provides the tool name).

---

Thanks a lot. I can confirm with the anthropic protocol Qwen 3.7 Max is working with Open WebUI if embedded via a LiteLLM Server to force the different protocols. In case somebody needs it:

1) Declare the API Key for Opencode in .env

2) Don't forget to define a variable for it also in docker-compose.yml

3) Entries for config.yaml (example models: MiMo V2.5 Pro and Qwen 3.7 Max):

```
 # Opencode
  # 1. Mimo -> OpenAI Format, base needs /v1, protocol is openai/
  - model_name: mimo-v2.5-pro
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/mimo-v2.5-pro
      api_base: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENCODE_API_KEY
      additional_drop_params: ["reasoningSummary"]

  # 2. Qwen -> Anthropic Format, base without /v1, protocol is anthropic/
  - model_name: qwen3.7-max
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/qwen3.7-max
      api_base: https://opencode.ai/zen/go
      api_key: os.environ/OPENCODE_API_KEY
```

This example works for a Zen subscription using Go models.

but yeah, you are right. Subagents should prevent us leaking too much context into the main agent context. Thereby this wouldnt really be that handy..

The idea may still not be a throw away. This "context limit filter" could also be helpful for when subagents pass information back to the main agent. Limiting them may prevent some subagents to pass unnecessary information and may force them to just provide the essentials. This may not be that important in relatively simple queries, but I think where RLM shines is when iteratively data needs to be extracted and (LLM) processed from many different places in the data source. Aligning the "subagent data return limit" with what is expected by the subagent query could benefit the overall processing of the found data.

Though we'd probaby want the "subagent data return limit" to be individually adjusted based on the task as on certain tasks more content needs to be returned than on others. Thereby this would ideally be a parameter in the subagent spawn process that the main agent should reason abount and decide for.

Also, leaning more towards the initial concept, the benefits of a "forced to decide on" context cap for its tools could still benefit the overall extraction capability of a single agent by optimizing how much context can be thrown into its window.

Dont mind this idea here though, it should just serve as inspiration.

Keymap layers can have a `priority` and dispatch order should be last added first, so the reverse order of when layers were added, then by priority, so higher priority should win. The dialog layers registered via `useBindings` should get a high `priority`, default is just 1 or 0 or something, so they can take `1000`. It's like a zindex basically.

Edit: I meant sort is by priority first, then newer registration first. So priority takes precedence.

This requires changes to both **OpenCode** and the underlying **AI SDK provider** to enable OpenCode to support `cache_control` for providers like Alibaba Cloud.

Here are my two repos:
- https://github.com/CaiDingxian/opencode/tree/feat/general_cache_control
- https://github.com/CaiDingxian/ai/tree/feat/openai-compatible-cache-control-v6

I've verified that it works and the cache hit rate looks good.

As for why I went with `openai-compatible` instead of the official AI SDK provider:
1. **`ai-sdk/alibaba` doesn't support parameter passthrough** — this means the official `preserve_thinking` parameter can't even be enabled, which is a blocker.
2. **I want generic support** for any provider that uses a similar `cache_control` format, not just Alibaba Cloud.

> @i-shm Thank you for your testing! > > The issue was when a CJK character (width 2, length 1) preceded a $skillname in the prompt, submission corrupted the reference — e.g. $w$webapp-testing instead of $webapp-testing. The extmark system stored positions as display-width offsets (Bun.stringWidth) but used them to slice() inputText with character offsets, so every preceding CJK char shifted the slice by one extra position. > > Fix: Refactored skills to use type: "skill" (matching the @ agent/file pattern) instead of type: "text" with kind: "skill". The extmark submission loop only processes type: "text" parts, so skills bypass the display-width-offset slice() entirely. The SkillPart & SkillPartInput type was added to the SDK to fix this. > > * Passed `bun typecheck` > > * Passed all tests in 'bun test` > > * Able to build locally and run properly > > * All user testing from before is working + trying CJK characters seems to work properly now as well > > > **TLDR: It should work now & the code quality is better!
